[Jumping Knowledge Networks](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/xu18c.html) aggregate intermediate states through concatenation, coordinatewise max, or node-specific LSTM attention, adapting effective neighborhood range. [ELMo](https://aclanthology.org/N18-1202/) instead learns task-specific softmax scalar weights shared across positions, plus an overall scale; its [ScalarMix implementation](https://docs.allennlp.org/v2.3.0/api/modules/scalar_mix/) optionally normalizes layers. Crucially, [dynamic layer aggregation](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/download/3772/3650) already includes position-specific feed-forward aggregation weights and routing-by-agreement. Thus, per-position softmax depth weighting has direct precedents. Applying it to channel-normalized NextItNet residual states suggests an architectural adaptation; novelty would require evidence for the particular conditioning or normalization mechanism. Unlike graph neighborhoods, NextItNet depths span progressively larger causal receptive fields.

Recommended controls: compare final-layer readout, uniform averaging, learned global ELMo-style weights, and position-dependent weights using identical residual states. Cross aggregation choice with prefix-summary conditioning on/off and normalization on/off. Include final-layer-plus-summary and uniform-mixture-plus-summary controls, giving them the same summary information and comparable parameter budgets; these test whether gains come from expanded context or additional capacity. Compare local-state-only, summary-only, and combined gates. Separate normalization of gate inputs from normalization of aggregated values, specifying channel axes and affine parameters because normalization implementations can differ.

Keep one jointly trained NextItNet per category, backbone depth/dilations, seeds, sampling, training budget, and evaluation fixed. Construct summaries causally with padding masks and read the final nonpadding position. Report macro validation HR@10 alongside gate entropy, depth usage by history length, and parameter/runtime costs. Replacing adaptive weights with their training-set mean at evaluation provides an additional sensitivity check, although retrained static controls provide stronger evidence.
